newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEST HAM BRACED FOR F.A. SANCTIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEST HAM BRACED FOR F.A. SANCTIONS.

text.p: Premier league West Ham risk punishment by the English F.A. because frustrated fans staged a pitch invasion at the end of Saturday's cup humiliation by Wrexham.
Around 400 spectators stormed the Upton Park ground after second division Wrexham knocked the relegation-haunted Londoners out of the F.A. Cup with a last minute winner in a third round replay.
The supporters continued their protest against club chairman Terrence Brown and his directors outside the stadium.
"As this time it happened after the final whistle we are hopeful the F.A. will take a reasonable view, but they might not," managing director Peter Storrie said.
"This is bound to be reported and we'll just have to wait and see if we face a charge. Any crowd disorder is a big concern for us."
West Ham were given an official warning by the F.A. five years ago after pitch invasions disrupted two home matches.
They were in trouble again last month when fans spilled on to the pitch to celebrate a goal.
West Ham fans plan another protest at the league game against Arsenal on Wednesday.
